recommended_phases.title: Phase 1 — Shared foundations (types, errors, unit-of-work)
recommended_phases.rationale: No module can compile without shared value types, error classes, and the transaction boundary. These are leaf dependencies with no inward deps.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2 — employee and policy modules
recommended_phases.rationale: Leaf domain modules depended on by validation and leave. Only depend on shared-types.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3 — audit and notification modules
recommended_phases.rationale: Cross-cutting side-effect modules consumed by leave; depend only on shared-db/shared-types.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4 — balance module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on shared-db/shared-types; required by validation and leave. Must exist before both.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 5 — validation module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on balance, policy, employee; consumed by leave orchestration.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 6 — leave module (service + controller + routes)
recommended_phases.rationale: Orchestrator depends on all prior modules; owns the transaction spanning request, balance, audit, notification.

app_notes: Application slice for the leave management module. Layering: presentation (routes/controllers) → application (services) → domain (models) → infrastructure (repositories, unit-of-work). Dependencies flow inward only; the leave module is the sole orchestrator and depends on balance, validation, policy, employee, audit, notification, and shared foundations — no module depends back on leave. All cross-module value types (LeaveStatus, LeaveType, AuditAction, NotificationStatus, EmploymentStatus, and the leave DTOs) live in src/shared/types/ per the shared-value-type rule; no single-purpose enum modules. Transaction ownership follows the settled decision: services own the unit of work via IUnitOfWork.withTransaction, repositories accept an optional client as the last parameter, and nested withTransaction reuses the supplied client. Every state-changing leave operation (create/submit/approve/reject/cancel) runs inside one transaction spanning the request row, balance mutation, and audit record, with notification emitted after commit. RBAC is enforced at route-level middleware (GP-005), never inline. The existing status/uptime modules are out of scope for this slice.

open_questions.question: How should leave days be counted for a date range (inclusive vs exclusive end date, and half-day handling)?
open_questions.impact: The derived day count feeds both balance deduction and validation; an inconsistent rule across sibling methods would violate the BR-001 anti-pattern.

open_questions.question: Should a controller layer be introduced for new modules, or should routes call services directly (as the existing uptime module does)?
open_questions.impact: Determines whether leave/balance/policy/employee/notification/audit modules each get a controller file, affecting file counts and phase sizing.
candidate_options: Introduce controller layer for all new modules
Routes call services directly, matching existing uptime pattern
Controller only for leave (orchestrator), direct for others

open_questions.question: Should BullMQ be added to package.json before implementing notification fanout/accrual jobs?
open_questions.impact: Notification delivery and accrual scheduling are declared in the architecture but BullMQ is not yet a dependency; affects whether notification is synchronous or queued.
candidate_options: Keep notifications synchronous (direct insert) for now

auth_contract: request.user: { id: string; role: UserRole } populated by a JWT bearer auth middleware that verifies the token and attaches the caller identity. UserRole = 'employee' | 'manager' | 'hr_admin'. RBAC is enforced by a requireRole(...) route-level guard, never inline: createRequest/submitRequest/cancelRequest require 'employee' (or the actor's own record); approveRequest/rejectRequest require 'manager' or 'hr_admin'; listRequests is role-scoped (employee sees own, manager sees team, hr_admin sees all).
error_response_contract: Standard error shape: { error: string; code: string }. Validation failure → HTTP 400 (ValidationError); authentication failure → 401 (UnauthorizedError); authorization failure → 403 (ForbiddenError); not found → 404 (NotFoundError); insufficient balance / invalid state transition → 409 (ConflictError).
